CLINICAL HISTORY: Gliosarcoma.

COMPARISON: 9/20/23 MR of the brain.

TECHNIQUE:

Multiplanar, multisequence MR imaging of the brain was performed
including axial T1, T2-weighted, axial FLAIR, axial diffusion-weighted
imaging (DWI), and post-contrast axial, coronal, and sagittal T1
sequences.

FINDINGS:

The patient has undergone a right parietal craniotomy. There is a
noted resection cavity with surrounding gliosis and mild FLAIR
hyperintensity extending into the adjacent parietal white matter.
There is stable enhancement along the margins of the resection
cavity with no new enhancing lesions identified. The T2-weighted
images show no significant change in the hyperintensity involving
the right parietal lobe and extending towards the occipital lobe.

MR perfusion analysis reveals relative cerebral blood volume
that is mildly elevated around the resection cavity, consistent
with residual neoplastic activity. No restricted diffusion is
observed to suggest acute infarction.

IMPRESSION:

1. Stable post-surgical changes in the right parietal region with
   persistent enhancement and no new enhancement.

2. Mildly increased perfusion surrounding the resection cavity
   indicating possible residual gliosarcoma.

END OF IMPRESSION:
